selected_answer: the chain rule is integral so both forward and backward pass works. It is the process used where a random bias plus input parameter has to pass to, so the model learns by computing the error, with gradient descent helping finding the local min, know how to nudge the parameters to minimize it. Without the chain rule, this highly optimized process wouldn't be easy to achieve, because it almost perfectly works against the nature of the input (matrices product), the flow for both direction, and extracting useful information nature to it's characteristics (like chain effect) working well with random-ish data, especially getting the answer to questions like "how to minimize the error". One thing to be careful about is the fine-tuning of hyper parameters and even the selection of the kind of gradient descent, to work against overfitting, or underfitting, or bad learning rate value, resulting to the process failing to minimize efficiently, or find the local minima reliably
